definition: An attack in which malicious instructions are embedded in input data (such as a webpage or document) to manipulate an AI system's behavior against its intended instructions.
details: Prompt injection is a significant security concern for LLM applications that process untrusted external content, such as agents that browse the web or read documents, since the model may struggle to distinguish trusted instructions from adversarial ones embedded in retrieved content.

explainer.lead: Prompt injection is an attack that embeds malicious instructions in input data, such as a webpage or document, to manipulate an AI system against its intended instructions. It matters for LLM applications that process untrusted external content.

tiers.eli5: It is like someone slipping a fake note into a stack of papers you were asked to read, hoping you follow it instead of your boss.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers worry about it most in agents that browse the web or read documents, where retrieved content may carry adversarial instructions. A pitfall is that the model may struggle to distinguish trusted instructions from adversarial ones in retrieved content.
tiers.paperLevel: Malicious instructions are embedded in input data and may override intended instructions. The core difficulty is the model's inability to reliably separate trusted instructions from adversarial embedded content.

explainer.example: A browsing agent reads a webpage containing hidden text telling it to ignore its task; the model may act on it instead of its original instructions.
